subject.title: fix(doctor): exit non-zero on final invalid config (#77804)

question: Should plain `openclaw doctor` retain its documented friendly-report exit behavior while automation uses `doctor --lint`, or should any final persisted-config validation error make plain doctor exit `1`?
rationale: Both behaviors are internally implementable, but changing the existing plain-command exit contract can break wrappers and operator workflows; repository source and tests cannot determine whether that compatibility change is desired.

options.title: Keep Plain Doctor Compatible
options.body: Keep plain doctor at its existing exit behavior and use the already-supported lint final-config check for CI and wrapper gating.

options.title: Make Plain Doctor Fail Closed
options.body: Intentionally adopt exit `1` for final invalid config, update the CLI documentation and compatibility expectations, and require built-CLI valid/invalid proof.

recommendation.title: Keep Plain Doctor Compatible
recommendation.body: Keep plain doctor at its existing exit behavior and use the already-supported lint final-config check for CI and wrapper gating.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the best available product and CLI contract decision owner, with recent adjacent doctor history and explicit repository governance responsibility.
